title: Conditional Volatility Targeting
one_line: Scaling exposure only when last month's volatility is in its top quintile (cut) or bottom quintile (raise), and staying unscaled otherwise, reduces drawdowns and tail risk in all 10 major equity markets with ~1/3 less turnover than conventional volatility targeting, which raised drawdowns in several markets.

findings.statement: Conventional vol targeting raised max drawdown 4-34% in UK, Canada, Australia, Hong Kong.
Conditional rule lowers drawdowns everywhere; Sharpe gains clearer for momentum than for market factors.

why.pattern: Volatility is persistent mainly at the extremes; scaling in between adds noise.

reported_results.headline: Scaling exposure only when last month's volatility is in its top quintile (cut) or bottom quintile (raise), and staying unscaled otherwise, reduces drawdowns and tail risk in all 10 major equity markets with ~1/3 less turnover than conventional volatility targeting, which raised drawdowns in several markets.

tradable_edge: Variant for liquidity_stress_overlay_es and for VOLATILITY_SIZING: scale only in the top/bottom quintile of prior volatility. Consistent with Cederburg et al.: plain vol targeting doesn't add edge.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Only the abstract / a secondary summary was reachable (SSRN is blocked from chat sessions); numbers not verified against the full paper.
